faq.a: Abdo is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُو, whose core sense is abdo; servant (of god).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdo?
faq.a: Abdo is associated with Arabic. Abdo is Arabic عَبْدُو (ʿAbdū), a familiar form of عَبْد (ʿAbd), meaning 'servant', used as a male given name.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُو is Arabic.
Abdo can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdo should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ب د is Quranic, but ʿAbd is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdo mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdo is rendered عبدو and carries the sense عبدو، بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdo mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdo is rendered عبدو and carries the sense عبدو، بنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-do. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Abdo?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdo, abdo. Script forms are عبدو, عَبْدُو, अब्दो.

faq.q: Is Abdo a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
